what: A want (spec/pages.md §6.14; spec/features/watch.md, 'Building a want by touch'): what to look for, then a price range dragged over the sales, ship or pickup with a radius, colour, size, how worn, which sites and how to be told, each set by touch; while it runs, how each site stands and what it has found so far. Pause and End.
frame: Who: the hunter setting up or tuning a search; the person clearing out, once, for one thing they need.
Came to do: say what they want, around what price, shipped or picked up, in what colour and size, then leave it running and stop searching by hand.
Where a mistake costs most: a top price set too high or a size left wrong, so alerts bring the wrong things or cost too much.
Ways out (spec/ways-out.md §6.12): Pause the want, or End it, one tap each; any site off; quiet hours; leave the app at any point.
In the loop: a new want is guessed from the words that started it and one tap starts it, because it sets a price; on a saved want every change saves at once with Undo and looks again.
decisions: Every value that changes which listings match is a control, not a typed field (Ben, words.md 2026-11-15: 'i can adjust my range etc. i can say shipped or pickup or both etc. color').

The price is a two-thumb range over the sales as dots (watch.md step 3): the top thumb is the most, the one ceiling for alerts; dots inside the range turn ink, so the range shows how many sales it would have caught.
'around $60' opens at $48 to $72, 20% either side (watch.md); with no price said, the most is the middle of the fair range and the low end 20% under it.
Ship, Pickup or Both is a three-way toggle drawn as equal chips, the iOS segmented control; pickup shows the radius as chips (5, 15, 25, 50 mi), Both and 15 mi by default (watch.md).
Colour is swatches with names, shown only when the colour is a choice: a Grey Fog Dunk has one colourway, so it gets no colour row (watch.md: only the chips that change which listings match appear).
Size is the system first, then the size, because a men's 10 is not a women's 10; only shoes and clothes get it.
How worn is four chips, new with tags to fair, read as 'at least'; good or better by default (watch.md).
A pick is a white chip with an ink outline, never a black one: one black button per view, and a pick is shape as well as color (Art. 5).
A new want is a hand-off: it sets a price, so the foot says exactly what it starts ('Watch for $80 or less') and nothing runs until the tap.
After the tap the sites answer one by one in the Where strip ('Just now'), with 'Found 6 so far' under it, and the foot says the person can leave and come back (watch.md, 'While the person is away').
A saved want opens on how its look stands, at the top: 'Looking on 4 sites', each logo with when it was checked, 'Behind' for a site whose check failed, and what it found so far.
A saved want saves each change at once with Undo, as iOS Settings does, and looks again at once (watch.md: a change re-runs the search).
Tell me is a two-row choice (Under the most, Any new one), the iOS list pattern, because both answers are short and exclusive.
Pause and End are gray pills, never the black one: End is the destructive act and it carries Undo.
Loading is the page's skeleton, failed says what did not load with Try again, and offline keeps the last copy under 'Waiting for signal' (app/src/buy/states.tsx), the same on every buy page.

A live find (the stage beat, ?live=1) sits right under what is being watched, above the price, because it is what the person is waiting for; it is the shared MatchCard with the read 'Under your price', since a find made live has no fair range behind it on stage, and its time is how long after listing it was found, from the site's own clock (Ben chose the alert inside the app, 08:06).
